goal: Plans are read from `~/mc/programs/<programme>/<project>/PLAN.json` (ruling 48, `docs/project/mc/mc-project.md`): `src/mc/plan-source.js` and `listPlans` in `src/mc/brief-collect.js` read that tree first, and a project there shadows a plan of the same name in a repository. A plan there names its repository in a top-level `repo` field. `mc project import` copies every plan on origin/main into the tree, and the active ones have been imported on this machine.

Whether a success criterion is met lives in the register (`~/mc/runner/projects/<project>.json`, `src/mc/register.js`), written by `mc project criterion met <project> <n>`, never in a pull request. The merge door (`criteriaDoor`) and every reader of a plan's done/unmet state read it from there.
contract: Where no plan is under `~/mc/programs/`, every reader returns exactly what it returns today: the repository plans on origin/main.
A plan under `~/mc/programs/` wins over the repository copy of the same project name. The repository copy stays where it is; nothing in this project deletes or changes a plan in a repository.
`met` already true in a plan file is carried into the register the first time the register sees the criteria; after that the file's `met` is not read.
The register's existing step fields, `mc step` and its output are unchanged. `listPlans`, `listProgrammes`, `findMainPlan`, `findPlan` and `planIn` keep their signatures; new options are optional.
out_of_scope: The verbs that write a plan (`mc project new`, `criterion add`, `step add`, `send`, `mc project <name>`) and the refusals at write time: project 2 of ruling 48.

Archiving and discarding a plan that lives under `~/mc/programs/`, removing the repository copies, `plan-merge.js`, `merge-boundary.js`'s `planBoundary`, `mc merge --docs` and the docs fast path: project 3. Until then a done plan under `~/mc/programs/` stays listed as done and is not archived, and its repository copy stays with it.
The `steps/` files and moving worktrees (`~/mc/plan/<programme>/`, `~/mc/step/<project>/`, `PLAN_HOME`, `STEP_HOME`) under `~/mc/programs/`.
`listProgrammes` and `listArchived`: programmes and closeouts are still read from the repositories.
The step prompt's quoting of the plan file's step `comments` instead of the register's (`planExcerpt`, `src/mc/run-plan.js`).

steps.title: The register holds the criteria's met
steps.done_when: `src/mc/register.js` exports `criteriaFromPlan`, `markCriterion` and `updateCriterion`, `seedEntry`, `reconcileEntry`, `normaliseEntry` and `applyEntry` carry `criteria`, the new cases in `tests/mc/register.test.js` pass with every existing one unchanged, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: All in `src/mc/register.js`; extend the header comment with one paragraph: the register also holds whether each success criterion is met (ruling 48) — the plan says what a criterion *is*, the register whether it *holds*; seeded from the file's `met` once, matched by the criterion's text, written by `mc project criterion met`.

1. Shape. An entry gains `criteria`: `null` (never seeded) or an array of `{ criterion, met, at }` — `criterion` the criterion's text, `met` a boolean, `at` an ISO string or `null`. In `normaliseEntry`, after `steps`: `criteria: Array.isArray(value.criteria) ? value.criteria.filter(plain).map((c) => ({ criterion: String(c.criterion ?? ''), met: c.met === true, at: typeof c.at === 'string' ? c.at : null })) : null`. (`plain` is already in the file.)

2. `export function criteriaFromPlan(plan)`: `(Array.isArray(plan?.success_criteria) ? plan.success_criteria : []).map((c) => ({ criterion: String(c?.criterion ?? ''), met: c?.met === true, at: null }))`. One-line JSDoc: the criteria as the plan file says them, the seed for an entry that has none.
3. `seedEntry`: add `criteria: criteriaFromPlan(record?.plan)` after `steps`.

4. `reconcileEntry`: compute `const criteria = reconcileCriteria(entry.criteria, record?.plan)` with a private helper: when `entry.criteria` is not an array return `criteriaFromPlan(plan)`; otherwise, for each plan criterion in order, take the first entry criterion with the same `criterion` text that has not been taken yet, else the file's own (`criteriaFromPlan` of that one criterion). Add `|| JSON.stringify(criteria) !== JSON.stringify(entry.criteria)` to `changed`, and `criteria` to the returned changed entry. The early `return { entry, changed: false, carried: [] }` for a moving running step stays as it is.

5. `applyEntry`: when `Array.isArray(entry.criteria)` and `Array.isArray(record.plan.success_criteria)`, the plan's `success_criteria` become `record.plan.success_criteria.map((c) => { const held = entry.criteria.find((e) => e.criterion === c?.criterion); return held ? { ...c, met: held.met } : c; })`, set on `plan` beside `steps` before `planSummary(plan)`. Matched by text, not index, because `run.js`'s `standing` applies an entry that has not been reconciled.

6. `export function markCriterion(entry, number, met, now = null)`: `number` is 1-based. When `entry.criteria` is not an array, or `number` is not an integer from 1 to its length, throw `new Error(`${entry.project}: no success criterion ${number} — the register holds ${n}`)` with `n` the length (0 for none). Otherwise return `{ ...entry, updated: now, criteria }` with that one criterion `{ ...c, met: met === true, at: now }`.

7. `export function updateCriterion({ root, project, number, met, read = realRead, write = realWrite, lock = realLock, now = null, append = realAppend, by = whoAmI })`: the shape of `updateStep` directly above it — under `lock`, `readEntry`, throw the same `not in the register` error when there is none, `markCriterion`, `write(registerPath(root, project), next)`, `logWrite(root, append, by, { event: 'criterion', project, number, from: <old met>, to: <new met> })`, return `next`.

8. `tests/mc/register.test.js`, new cases in the file's style: `normaliseEntry` keeps `criteria` and gives `null` without it; `seedEntry` seeds `criteria` from the file's `met`; `reconcileEntry` seeds `criteria` on an entry that has `null`, keeps a held `met: true` when the file says `false`, takes the file's for a new text, drops a removed one, and reports `changed`; `applyEntry` with a held `met: true` turns a plan whose steps are all done from `unmet` to `done` (`status`), and leaves a criterion it holds no text for as the file says; `markCriterion` sets `met` and `at` and throws for 0, for one past the end and for `criteria: null`; `updateCriterion` with in-memory `read`/`write`/`lock`/`append` writes the entry and appends one `criterion` log line.
9. `mc gate tests/mc/register.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

instruction: 1. New `src/mc/commands/project.js`, in the style of `src/mc/commands/step.js` (header comment, `run(argv, deps = {})` returning an exit code, `usage()`). Header: `mc project` is where mc's own verbs over a project live (ruling 48, `docs/project/mc/mc-project.md`); for now it records whether a success criterion is met — the register's, never a pull request's. Imports: `parseStepEnv`, `readEntry`, `updateCriterion` from `../register.js`, `workRoot` from `../paths.js`, `scanArgs` from `./flags.js`.

2. `run`: `stdout`, `stderr`, `env`, `root = deps.root || workRoot(env)`, `now` and the `io` object of `read`/`write`/`lock` built exactly as at the top of `step.js`'s `run`. `scanArgs(argv, { booleans: [], strictValues: [] })`; on `error` print `mc: <error>` and the usage, return 2. Positional `[noun, verb, ...rest]`: anything but `criterion` followed by `met` or `unmet` → usage on stderr, return 2. `rest` is `<project> <n>` or `<n>` alone; with `<n>` alone the project is `parseStepEnv(env.MC_STEP)?.project`, and when there is none print `mc: which project? mc project criterion met <project> <n>, or MC_STEP in a runner session` and return 2. `<n>` that is not `/^\d+$/u` → `mc: <n> is not a criterion number — 1 is the plan's first`, return 2. `readEntry(root, project, io)` null → `mc: <project> is not in the register`, return 1. Then `updateCriterion({ root, project, number, met: verb === 'met', now, ...io })`; print `mc: <project> criterion <n> — met` (or `— not met`), return 0; a thrown error prints `mc: <message>` and returns 1.

A success criterion holds: the register, not the plan file`, padded like its neighbours. Run `node --test tests/mc/help.test.js`; if it names another place a verb must be listed, add it there.

5. `tests/mc/commands/project.test.js` in the style of `tests/mc/commands/step.test.js`, with an in-memory register (`read`/`write`/`lock` deps, an entry holding `criteria: [{ criterion: 'a', met: false, at: null }, { criterion: 'b', met: false, at: null }]`): `criterion met p 2` → exit 0, the written entry's second criterion `met: true`, `at` the injected now, and the output line; `criterion unmet p 2` after it → `met: false`; `criterion met 1` with `env.MC_STEP = 'p:0'` writes `p`; without `MC_STEP` → exit 2; `criterion met p 3` → exit 1 naming `no success criterion 3`; `criterion met p x` → exit 2; an unknown project → exit 1; `frobnicate` → exit 2.

instruction: 1. `canon/roles/step.md`: the paragraph beginning `You never change the plan` becomes: `You never change the plan file. A success criterion you measured with its check is recorded with mc project criterion met <n>; on the last step every criterion is, or the PR does not land. Your step's state lives in mc's register, written by mc step. Anything the next reader needs that the code does not show: the PR body and mc step note "…".` (keep the backticks around verbs as the file does). In the `mc merge` list: `plan-trespass` becomes `undo every change to the plan file, commit, push, run mc merge again.`; `unmet-criteria` becomes `you are the plan's last step and a success criterion is not met in the register: run its check and mc project criterion met <n> for each you measured, then mc merge again; one you cannot measure is mc step failed --reason naming it.` followed by the existing sentences from `Every check is yours` to the end of that item, unchanged.

A success criterion you measured with its check is recorded with \`mc project criterion met <n>\` — the register, not the file; on the plan's last step \`mc merge\` refuses the pull request until every criterion is met there.` Keep the line wrapping style of the array.

Extend that comment by one sentence saying the criteria's `met` is the exception.

5. `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` line ~363: the assertion becomes `/Your plan is at `docs\/project\/p\/x\/PLAN\.json`/u`. Run `node --test tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` and update only assertions that quote a sentence this step rewrote. If a test checks role files (`grep -rl "step.md" tests`), run it too.

steps.title: mc project import
steps.done_when: `mc project import` lists, and `mc project import --apply` writes, every repository plan on origin/main that is not yet under `~/mc/programs/`, with `repo` set, refusing nothing it would overwrite; `tests/mc/commands/project.test.js` covers it; and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: 1. `src/mc/commands/project.js`: a second form, `mc project import [--apply]` (add `--apply` to `scanArgs`'s `booleans`). Deps, injectable for the tests: `repos` (default `defaultRepos(env)` from `../brief-collect.js`), `listRepoPlans` (default from `../brief-collect.js`), `programs` (default `programsPlans` from `../plan-source.js`), `home` (default `programsHome(env)` from `../paths.js`), `fetch` (default: `spawnSync('git', ['-C', repo.path, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin'])` per repo, its status ignored), `writeText` (default: `mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true })` then `writeFileSync(tmp)` and `renameSync(tmp, path)`, with `tmp` = `${path}.${process.pid}.tmp`).

2. For each repo whose `join(repo.path, '.git')` exists: `fetch(repo)`, then `listRepoPlans(repo)`. Keep a record when `!record.legacy && record.plan` and its `project` is not among `programs()` projects; a record with `problems.length` is reported `skip <repo>:<programme>/<project> — does not read: <first problem>` and not imported. For each kept record, the new text: parse the original text (`git show origin/main:<path>` is already in `record` as `plan`), and write `JSON.stringify({ schema, version, repo: repo.name, ...rest }, null, 2) + '\n'` where `{ schema, version, ...rest } = record.plan` — `repo` third, everything else in the plan's order. Run it through `readPlanText`; if it has problems, report `skip … — <first problem>`. Target `join(home, record.programme, record.project, PLAN_FILE)` (`PLAN_FILE` from `../plan-source.js`). Two repositories holding one project name: the first in `repos` order is imported, the second reported `skip <repo>:<…> — <project> is <first repo>'s`.

3. Output: without `--apply`, one line per plan `would import <repo>:<programme>/<project> → <target>` and a last line `mc project import --apply to write them`; with `--apply`, `imported …` per plan. When nothing is kept, print `nothing to import` and return 0. A target that exists is never written (it is a programs plan by then and was filtered; the check is for a file that is not valid JSON — report `skip … — <target> exists`). Return 0, or 1 when a write throws (print `mc: <message>`). The register is not touched: its entry is brought up to the new `path` by the next reader (`reconcileEntry`).

4. `usage()` gains `mc project import [--apply]        copy every plan on origin/main that is not under ~/mc/programs/ there, with its repo — without --apply it shows what would go`. `src/mc/help-text.js` gains the same line under the `mc project criterion` line.

5. Tests in `tests/mc/commands/project.test.js`, every dep injected, `home` a temp directory: two repos, one plan each plus a legacy record and a record with problems; dry run prints two `would import` lines and writes nothing; `--apply` writes two files whose JSON has `repo` third and otherwise equals the plan, and whose `readPlanText` problems are `[]`; a project already in `programs()` is not imported; the same project in both repos is imported from the first and skipped in the second; nothing kept prints `nothing to import`.
6. `mc gate tests/mc/commands/project.test.js tests/mc/help.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. Do not run the import against the real `~/mc/programs/` in this step.

steps.title: Import on this machine, and plans are written under ~/mc/programs/
steps.done_when: `~/mc/programs/` holds every active plan of memoro and memoro-cli, `canon/roles/_plan-writing.md` and `docs/project/README.md` say plans are written there, all three success criteria are met in the register through `mc project criterion met`, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: 1. From this worktree, on this machine: `node src/mc-cli.js project import` and read the list: it must name every `PLAN.json` that `git -C <repo> ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- docs/project` shows in `~/memoro` (or the memoro checkout `defaultRepos` names) and in this repository, minus any already under `~/mc/programs/`. Then `node src/mc-cli.js project import --apply`. Then `node src/mc-cli.js project import` again must print `nothing to import`. A `skip` line for a plan that does not read is reported in the PR body, not fixed.

2. `node src/mc-cli.js status plans-in-mc` must print a `plan` row ending in `programs/mc/plans-in-mc/PLAN.json (origin/main)`, and `node src/mc-cli.js step plans-in-mc` must still show this project's steps with their states (the register entry follows the new path through `reconcileEntry` on the next read).

3. `canon/roles/_plan-writing.md`: the `**Where:**` item becomes: plans live in mc, not in a repository (ruling 48): `~/mc/programs/<programme>/<project>/PLAN.json`, with a top-level `"repo": "memoro"` or `"memoro-cli"` naming where the steps run. Write it to a temporary file beside it, validate, then `mv` it into place: the runner reads the directory, so a plan whose first unfinished step is `ready` is run as soon as it is there, and moving it in is the handover. No branch, no pull request. The `**Validate before pushing:**` item becomes `**Validate before moving it in:**` with the same command, and its last sentence becomes: ``mc status <project>`` shows it. In the `**Overall:**` item, `All frozen: a step session writes only met.` becomes `All frozen: a step session records a met criterion with mc project criterion met, never in the file.`; and in the `A check the last step's own branch cannot reach` item, `every criterion is met` becomes `every criterion is met in the register`. Keep the rest.

4. `docs/project/README.md`: at the top of `## What a PLAN.json is`, one paragraph: since `plans-in-mc` a plan lives under `~/mc/programs/<programme>/<project>/PLAN.json` with a `repo` field, and a plan of the same name in this directory is shadowed by it and no longer read; the copies here go with project 3 of ruling 48. In the `success_criteria` bullet, add: whether a criterion is met is the register's, written by `mc project criterion met <project> <n>`; the file's `met` is read once, when the register first sees the criteria.

5. Run the three success criteria's checks from this branch. For each that passes: `node src/mc-cli.js project criterion met plans-in-mc <n>`. Then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.
